title: China Southwest Airlines 4509
summary: Flight 4509, a Tupolev Tu-154M flying Chengdu-Wenzhou, was on approach when the crew extended flaps at 1,000 m; seconds later the nose dropped abruptly and the aircraft disintegrated in mid-air before crashing into high ground near Rui'an and exploding, killing all 61 aboard. The investigation found incorrect self-locking locknuts had been installed in the elevator system without maintenance crews noticing; the nuts worked loose in flight, leaving the elevator uncontrollable and disabling the pitch channel.
probable_cause: Incorrect self-locking locknuts installed in the elevator operating system went unnoticed by maintenance crews and spun off during the flight, leaving the elevator uncontrollable and disabling the pitch channel, causing the crash.

title: 1999 F-117A shoot-down
summary: On March 27, 1999, during NATO air operations against Yugoslavia in the Kosovo War, a Yugoslav Army air defense unit shot down a U.S. Air Force F-117A Nighthawk stealth fighter with a surface-to-air missile near Ruma. The aircraft flew the same bombing route for several consecutive days, making it predictable to visual tracking by Yugoslav defenders. The pilot, Lieutenant Colonel Darrell Zelko, ejected safely as the F-117 tumbled out of control and was rescued eight hours later by U.S. search and rescue forces.
probable_cause: A Yugoslav Army air defense unit equipped with an S-125 Neva surface-to-air missile successfully targeted the F-117A stealth aircraft by tracking it visually from its repeated takeoff base route and launching missiles at the predicted crossing point. Repeated bombing runs on the same track over multiple days negated the stealth advantage. Missile detonation caused significant structural damage and loss of control, forcing the pilot to eject.

summary: Flight 1420 was diverted from its originally assigned runway due to a wind shear alert and wind direction change. The crew requested runway 4R for a headwind during landing, but due to the aircraft's weather radar having a narrow forward-facing field of view and heavy precipitation causing radar attenuation, the crew could not see a severe thunderstorm approaching the airport during their turn. The aircraft touched down on the wet runway, but the pilots failed to arm the automatic spoiler system. Without spoilers deployed, the aircraft could not stop and overran the runway by 800 feet, striking the ILS localizer array and approach light structure.
probable_cause: Runway overrun caused by failure to deploy spoilers on landing, resulting in loss of landing gear effectiveness and inability to stop within runway confines. title: Pakistan Naval Air Arm Atlantique shootdown
summary: A Pakistan Navy Breguet Atlantique maritime patrol aircraft was shot down by an Indian Air Force MiG-21 fighter over the Rann of Kutch border region. summary: FedEx Express Flight 087, an MD-11F cargo aircraft, took off from Shanghai and encountered moderate turbulence at cruise altitude. Autopilot disengaged at 15:33 with spurious airspeed warning. The crew attempted to unify air data computers to resolve airspeed disagreement. On approach, the aircraft could not extend flaps to 50 degrees with excessive landing speed. At 15:55:04 the aircraft landed on runway 07 and rolled down the entire runway length before plunging into Subic Bay. Both pilots escaped with minor injuries. Clogged pitot drain holes and crew failure to respond to incorrect airspeed indications contributed.
probable_cause: The flight crew failed to respond appropriately to incorrect airspeed indications and recognize the correct airspeed source, combined with clogged pitot tube drain holes.

title: 1999 South Dakota Learjet crash
summary: A Learjet 35 departed Orlando bound for Dallas with two pilots and four passengers. At 13:27 UTC while climbing through 23000 feet, the aircraft lost cabin pressure, incapacitating all six occupants with hypoxia. The aircraft continued climbing on autopilot past assigned altitude, failed to make the required westward turn toward Dallas, and continued northwest for approximately four hours and 1500 miles. At 17:10 UTC the engines wound down at fuel exhaustion, and the aircraft subsequently entered an uncontrolled spiral descent and crashed near Aberdeen in Edmunds County, South Dakota.
probable_cause: Loss of cabin pressurization early in the flight incapacitated all occupants through hypoxia. The plane had several unresolved maintenance issues related to cabin pressure in the months leading up to the crash.

events.text: Learjet 35 N47BA departed Orlando International Airport at 13:19 UTC with 5300 lb of Jet A for four hours and 45 minutes of flight.

The aircraft failed to make the required westward turn toward Dallas over North Florida and continued on its northwestern course for almost four hours and 1500 miles.

title: EgyptAir 990

agencies.name: Egyptian Ministry of Civil Aviation's Civil Aviation Agency

summary: EgyptAir Flight 990, a Boeing 767 flying from Los Angeles to Cairo via New York, crashed into the Atlantic Ocean south of Nantucket on 31 October 1999, killing all 217 aboard. The NTSB concluded the aircraft departed normal cruise flight and dived into the ocean as a result of relief First Officer Gameel Al-Batouti's flight control inputs after he disengaged the autopilot and pushed the elevators nose-down while repeating 'I rely on God,' while Egypt's Civil Aviation Agency maintained the crash was caused by mechanical failure.
probable_cause: The NTSB's probable cause was the aircraft's departure from normal cruise flight and impact with the ocean as a result of relief First Officer Al-Batouti's flight control inputs, for which no specific reason could be determined; Egypt's ECAA independently concluded the crash was caused by mechanical failure.

factors.evidence: The NTSB found that the cause of the accident was the airplane's departure from normal cruise flight and subsequent impact with the Atlantic Ocean 'as a result of the relief first officer's flight control inputs'.
At 1:49:45 he disengaged the autopilot; the autopilot-disengagement warning was not heard on the CVR, indicating that the autopilot was disengaged manually.
Three seconds later, the throttles for both engines were reduced to idle, and both elevators were moved 3 degrees nose down.
The flight data recorder reflected that the elevators moved into a split condition, with the left elevator up and the right elevator down, during the abrupt maneuvers to recover from the dive.
The stress placed on the airframe caused structural integrity to fail at approximately 10,000 feet, with the left engine and other debris separating from the aircraft.

events.text: At 1:48, with the aircraft at its 33,000-foot cruising altitude, Captain El-Habashi left the cockpit for the lavatory, leaving relief First Officer Al-Batouti alone at the controls.
At 1:48:39 relief First Officer Al-Batouti began repeating 'I rely on God' in Egyptian Arabic.
At 1:49:45 the autopilot was disengaged manually, without triggering the disconnect warning on the cockpit voice recorder.
Three seconds after the autopilot disengaged, the throttles for both engines were reduced to idle and both elevators were moved three degrees nose down.

Radar data showed the aircraft entering a steep climb from 16,000 back to 25,000 feet between 1:50:38 and 1:51:15, with the elevators moving into a split condition of left elevator up and right elevator down.
At 1:51:15 the aircraft entered a second steep dive at around 20,000 feet per minute, and structural integrity failed at approximately 10,000 feet before impact with the ocean at 1:52 am.

notes: NTSB and Egypt's ECAA reached different conclusions about the cause; no motive for the relief first officer's actions was established.

title: TAESA 725
summary: TAESA Flight 725, a 29-year-old McDonnell-Douglas DC-9-31, departed Uruapan for Mexico City on November 9, 1999 at 18:59 local time with 13 passengers and 5 crew. The aircraft crashed into an avocado field 3.3 miles south of the runway, killing all 18 on board.

title: Si Fly 325
summary: ATR 42 on shuttle flight from Rome to Pristina for UN aid workers struck mountain during approach on November 12, 1999. Investigation revealed crew experiencing fatigue from high roster failed to execute appropriate approach procedure and deviation was not detected. ATC personnel accidentally forgot to track flight during approach and did not pay adequate attention during radar vectoring. Combined with faulty GPWS warning system that company had postponed repairing, aircraft failed to clear terrain and crashed.

title: Korean Air Cargo 8509
summary: During dark takeoff from London Stansted, the captain's inertial navigation unit failed, providing erroneous roll data to his attitude director indicator. The aircraft entered clouds at 400 feet and banked left into an unrecoverable attitude. The flight engineer called out the instrument failure, but the captain ignored the comparator alarm and continued commanding a steeper left bank, crashing 55 seconds after takeoff.
probable_cause: Failure of the captain's inertial navigation unit providing erroneous roll data to his attitude indicator, combined with inadequate crew resource management by the first officer who failed to challenge the captain's control inputs.

events.text: It was dark when the plane took off from London Stansted Airport with the captain flying.

At 18:38, 55 seconds after take-off, Flight 8509's left-wing dragged along the ground and the aircraft plunged into the ground at a 40-degree pitch down and 90-degree left bank attitude.
